thread.title: Analysis finds Fairfax County pandemic grant programs aided small business survival
thread.title_full: Analysis finds Fairfax County pandemic grant programs aided small business survival

author: l. f. perez
title: Analysis finds Fairfax County pandemic grant programs aided small business survival
text:
Fairfax County’s Department of Economic Initiatives launched two relief programs, RISE and PIVOT, during the COVID-19 pandemic to support small businesses. According to an independent analysis by the George Mason University Center for Regional Analysis, these programs helped thousands of local businesses remain open and retain jobs.
The RISE program was funded through the federal CARES Act, while the PIVOT Recovery Grant Program received support from the American Rescue Plan. Together, they distributed nearly $70 million to more than 5,400 small businesses and nonprofit organizations in Fairfax County.
The evaluation found that businesses receiving grants were more likely to stay in operation compared to similar businesses that did not get assistance. The study estimated a nearly 6% increase in business survival rates among participants. Survey results showed that 94% of grant recipients who responded are still operating, with most reporting improved long-term stability due to the funding.
The analysis also indicated broader economic benefits. Grant-related spending boosted total economic activity in Fairfax County by $95.5 million and increased regional output by almost $64 million. The programs supported 572 jobs and provided about $50 million in wages and benefits.
Business owners credited the grants as essential during a difficult period. One recipient said, “I would have had to close without this support,” adding, “It truly made a difference and saved my business.”
The county attributes the success of these programs to rapid implementation, targeted eligibility criteria, and clear outreach efforts that ensured federal relief funds reached local employers efficiently. These actions align with Fairfax County’s ongoing strategies for economic resilience and workforce support.
For more information or access to the full impact analysis, contact the Department of Economic Initiatives.
